title: Two park payments reached the wrong artwork fund. One remains untraced.

beats.text: Two payments went into San Francisco’s downtown artwork fund by mistake.

visual.sub: Two payments went into the Downtown C-3 Artwork Fund in error

beats.text: Recreation and Park used the larger payment for the North Beach pool, clubhouse and bocce court.

visual.kicker: The records distinguish appropriate park spending from unresolved cash

beats.text: The Controller called that spending appropriate. The other payment was still unspent.
That money was intended for open space near Castro Street.

visual.kicker: The Controller later described a broader year-end accounting problem

beats.text: A report issued in 2020 still described the payment as unspent.

visual.kicker: The Controller later described a broader year-end accounting problem

beats.text: The Controller also said unspent artwork fees had rolled into the General Fund by mistake.

visual.kicker: The Controller later described a broader year-end accounting problem

beats.text: New receipts went to a special revenue fund.

visual.kicker: The Controller later described a broader year-end accounting problem

beats.text: Across two editions, the reported balances differ by $1,860,801.
The later year balances internally. It gives no breakdown that traces the Castro payment.

visual.kicker: The next report starts from a different aggregate balance
visual.text: What the balances can tell us

beats.text: The final transfer and project ledger would show what happened to that payment.

visual.kicker: The next report starts from a different aggregate balance
